request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The audit now records the figure changes the request asks for, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`. This was a server-only change; the front end and database are untouched.

**How it works:** a new service, `rollup/Rollups.java`, works out each person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's two totals, the same way the screen does. That includes showing `n/a` when a grade has no rate today and no claim has a fixed figure, and leaving `n/a` people out of the due-total. Each change takes these figures just before it writes and compares them just after its own audit line:
- It writes one `ROLLUP … person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order they were added. A newly added person always gets a line.
- It then writes `TOTALS … claimed-total=… due-total=…` if either sheet total moved.
- Nothing is written if no figure moved. The lines are only written once the change commits, so a refused change still writes nothing.

The spec writes `person=<name>` in the ROLLUP lines rather than the request's `name=<name>`, so I followed the spec.

**Where it's applied:** adding, editing, opening, settling and voiding claims; adding and editing people; setting a rate; taking a statement; and changing the sheet's today.

**Other changes:**
- **Changing today now requires a signed-in user.** The `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/today` endpoint now requires the `X-User` header so the lines can carry `by=`. The screen already sends it on every request once someone has signed in.
- **Due calculation moved.** The code that works out what's due on a claim moved from `ClaimService` into a new `claim/Dues.java` so the rollup service can use it too. `ClaimService.figure` still exists and passes the call through to it.
